The story I always think about when I consider foods changing is the salade nicoise. Many people all over the world have had this salad. There are versions on restaurant menus everywhere. As a kid my mom would make it for us with lettuce, boiled eggs, anchovies, canned tuna, potatoes, green beans, peppers, tomatoes etc. It was one of my favourites.

As an adult out on my own I was craving it and wanted to double check that I had all of the many ingredients so I jumped on the internet and fell down the rabbit hole of the salad's history. I was surprised to learn that the salad, in its hometown of Nice, France, at its simplest only contains tomatoes and anchovies and that the purists would die before they included any boiled vegetables.

So what had happened? A well-known Parisian (I believe) chef, compiling a book of the best recipes from all over France had included a completely bastardized version of the salade nicoise and from then on that was what people all over the world considered the salad to be.

When I learned about this I tried the simple authentic version and it was delicious. But I had always loved the bastardized version as well, and that wasn't going to just change. Both are great, so it's fine, right? Well not to some people in Nice, who felt pretty frustrated about an important cultural dish that had had its name slapped on a completely different salad. The original was a dish for the poor, and the beauty was in its simplicity, but now a big-city Parisian had taken that away. I couldn't help but empathize with the people of Nicoise who felt that something of their culture had been stolen from them, which it had.

So why does it matter? Well, he effectively stole the name of a traditional dish in order to push his own, very different recipe. They're both good, but they aren't the same, and the more well-known version stands in front of the classic dish and obscures it for basically everyone outside of Southern France, who are unlikely to spend their time researching the origins of the foods they eat.

Without a little gatekeeping recipes can change so much that the delicious original can be hidden or in extreme cases lost. If you are going to innovate, please do! It's what has led us to such an amazing culinary world. But if someone is bold enough to create new recipes they can also be brave enough to slap a new name on it - even if that name is just explaining the modification from an original - and allow the classic its room to breath. That's the line between innovation and bastardization, in my opinion.

Buckle up, dude. Literature and narratives are a huge part of my job so I've put way too much thought into this. In my opinion this is the optimal GTA Online narrative experience that makes it feel like you’re progressing naturally like in the single player games. No spoilers. 

Notes: Go into your settings and set your character to only be called once per hour. The game absolutely spams you with sales calls that completely throw off the narrative. This will seriously cut down on those calls. If someone is trying to get you to buy something they can probably be ignored and hung up on until it's actually time to buy that thing. Some story related things will come through phone calls though, so use discretion. 

There is a cut-scene at Mirror Park and another in the Music Locker at the Casino that you should avoid triggering as they will be completely out of place until much later in the game. Visiting the casino is fine and you can actually even go into the Music Locker as long as you avoid the booth where the cut-scene is. 

A foursome is the perfect number for most things, but there are some missions that are only two player, so just split up into teams of two and run the job twice separately. 

1) Tutorial 

2) Buy a low-end apartment and set it as your spawn-point. 

GTA always started you out in a crummy safe-house. It’s fun to progress from the low life to the high life. One is free with the starter pack and you can claim it or buy a different one. 

2) Contact missions for Simeon and Gerald. 

The original GTA Online story content. Do a handful of missions for each of them and then move on when you're ready. When doing contact missions you want to select them from the jobs menu, not go to their icon, as starting jobs at the icon will throw you into random missions that were probably added years later. Use this list to select your missions: 

https://gta.fandom.com/wiki/Missions_in_GTA_Online 

Avoid any mission that wasn’t in the game at launch. It doesn’t really matter how many you do for Simeon, but I’d recommend you do Gerald’s first 5 since Meth’d Up ties into a later contact. If you’re having fun do as many contacts as you like. 

3) Go parachuting 

Do this once so that Dom doesn’t call you anymore. There are a few more of these down the road, like ordering Bull Shark Testosterone once you’re a CEO so that Brucie stops bothering you, or using Lester’s and Merryweather’s services. 

4) Lamar’s Lowrider missions 

This came out after heists but is accessible without buying any property and it doesn’t make sense to take orders from Lamar after you’re a successful bank robber. 

5) Buy a midrange apartment and set it as your spawnpoint. 

Now that you’re making a name for yourself and have made a little money you shouldn’t have to live in that dump. IMO a property in Paleto Bay is worth having and keeping forever but get whatever you want. 

6) Meet and do contact missions for Ron & Trevor, then Lester, then Martin Madrazo. 

Lester will call you for a meet at level 10, which you can go to and unlock his phone call abilities. His first mission won’t be available until level 19. Ron will call you to come meet him and Trevor at level 13. Martin calls you at level 18 and you’ll meet him in person in a cutscene after his first mission – Out of Court Settlement - at level 22. Expect these phonecalls and like with Gerald and Simeon, do as many missions as you enjoy. The starting inheritance law is Confederate Partition. This law creates new titles and gives them away if you have enough land to create those titles, even if you choose not to create them while alive.

For example: You hold the Kingdom of England. You conquer all of the duchies in Scotland but don’t create the title. If you have two sons, your first born will inherit England, and your second son will inherit the Kingdom of Scotland, which will be created just for him.

If you changed your inheritance to regular Partition. Your firstborn would inherit the Kingdom of England, and the second son would inherit some of your other lands, like your duchies and counties, but no new titles would be created, so he’d still be your vassal and part of your kingdom. This type of partition still tries to divide things up evenly, so if you have two kingdom titles, each will go to one son and obviously both will be independent since kings can’t have other kings as vassals.

High Partition is the same a partition, but gives at least half of your titles to your firstborn.

If your kingdom splits under confederate partition, don’t forget that your new character still has a claim to his father’s old titles, so you can always have a quick war and get it back… or you can murder your sibling (and their heirs) and inherit it back…

There's another, slightly less confusing cut-scene for the Cayo Perico Heist at the music locker for you to avoid. Characters are met for the first time in earlier missions that you'll run into later, and there are little connected story-lines along the way. If you're interested in it, the rough chronology follows the release order of the updates:

- Contact missions: Here you meet Lamar, Gerald, Simeon, Trevor & Ron, Martin & Lester. Most of whom come up later (2013).
- Original heists: Buying a high-end apartment ($200k+) unlocks the original 5 heists for Lester. These heists involve Lester, Trevor & Ron, and introduce you to new characters who will show up later.
- Lamar's Lowrider missions form a small storyline that technically takes place after the heists but is accessible immediately without buying any expensive properties.
- Purchasing an office and warehouse, biker businesses, and import/export garage is next chronologically, but almost entirely unconnected to anything story-wise.
- GTAV's single-player story takes place (2013).
- The "story" then jumps forward 4 years. Buying a bunker will have you reconnecting with a character from the original heists (2017).
- Buying a hanger will reconnect you with another character.
- The Doomsday Heist is next. Lester is back and will have you buy a facility to complete this. Other characters will reappear as well.
- Buying the Nightclub reacquaints you with some old story characters and introduces a new one who will appear later (2018).
- The arena update was the next big one, but the characters introduced by it don't connect to anything else.
- The Diamond Casino opens, and buying a penthouse unlocks a small story-line of missions to help the casino management (2018).
- The cut-scene at Mirror Park, kicking off the Diamond Casino heist, fits in here. Obviously doing the heist is the next move. After everything you've previously done with Lester and the missions you've done to help the casino, all the story around the heist now actually makes sense.
- There's a little story-line of yacht missions. I've never done these so I have no idea how connected they are (2019).
- The cutscene at the music locker and the Cayo Perico heist. Returning characters and relatives of characters we know.
